intro: Ljubljana rewards visitors with a compact old town, riverside cafés and easy day trips. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; the city runs on buses plus a small electric tourist train.
City buses use the Urbana card; buy it at kiosks or with the Urbana app.
Taxis are metered; ride apps like Bolt and Uber operate in Ljubljana.
Driving is easy outside rush hour; parking in the centre is limited and paid.
The centre is very walkable and bike-friendly; bike share and rental shops exist.
No ferry service; boats run on the Ljubljanica river for tours.

ljubljana_castle.name: Ljubljana Castle
ljubljana_castle.price_text: Castle grounds free · exhibitions and tower charged, check on the day
ljubljana_castle.hours: Grounds open daily · indoor sights roughly 09:00–20:00 in summer, shorter in winter
ljubljana_castle.tip: Walk up from the Old Town in about 15 minutes, or take the funicular from Krekov trg.

triple_bridge.name: Triple Bridge
triple_bridge.tip: Stand on the middle span and look back at Prešeren Square for the classic photo.

preseren_square.name: Prešeren Square
preseren_square.tip: The square is the city's living room; meet here and watch the light change on the pink Franciscan church.

st_nicholas_cathedral.name: St. Nicholas Cathedral
st_nicholas_cathedral.price_text: Free entry · small fee for the crypt, check on the day
st_nicholas_cathedral.hours: Daily, roughly 07:00–19:00; closed to tourists during Mass
st_nicholas_cathedral.tip: Look up at the baroque frescoes and the bronze side doors added for the pope's 1996 visit.

national_museum.name: National Museum of Slovenia
national_museum.price_text: Modest entry fee, check on the day · free on some days
national_museum.tip: See the famous Ljubljana Marshes wooden wheel, one of the oldest in the world.

dragon_bridge.name: Dragon Bridge
dragon_bridge.tip: The dragon is the city symbol; rub a dragon's nose for luck, as locals joke.

struklji.name: Štruklji
struklji.price_text: ≈ EUR 5–10 per portion at a typical restaurant
struklji.hours: Served at most traditional restaurants, roughly 11:00–22:00
struklji.tip: Try the rolled dumplings sweet with walnuts or savoury with tarragon; ask what is fresh that day.

central_market.name: Central Market (Pogačarjev trg)
central_market.price_text: Free to browse · food priced per item
central_market.hours: Market roughly Mon–Sat mornings; Friday food market in warmer months
central_market.tip: Come before noon for produce; Friday's open-air food stalls are the local favourite.

funicular_viewpoint.name: Castle Tower viewpoint
funicular_viewpoint.price_text: Tower entry charged, check on the day
funicular_viewpoint.tip: Climb the tower for the best 360° view over the red roofs and the Alps on a clear day.

boat_tour.name: Ljubljanica river boat tour
boat_tour.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–15 for a short cruise, check on the day
boat_tour.tip: A short cruise under the bridges is a relaxed way to see the Old Town from the water.

metelkova.name: Metelkova mesto
metelkova.price_text: Free to walk · drinks and events priced separately
metelkova.hours: Open area always; bars and clubs mostly evenings
metelkova.tip: An old army barracks turned squatter art quarter; go in daylight to see the murals, at night for music.

tivoli_park.name: Tivoli Park
tivoli_park.tip: Walk the tree-lined promenade up to the Rožnik hill for a green escape from the centre.

old_town_walk.name: Old Town riverside walk
old_town_walk.tip: Follow the Ljubljanica from the Triple Bridge south past cafés and small galleries.

free_walking_tour.name: Free walking tour of the centre
free_walking_tour.price_text: Free to join · tip the guide
free_walking_tour.hours: Usually one or two departures daily, check on the day
free_walking_tour.tip: A good first-hour orientation; meet near Prešeren Square and tip what you feel it was worth.

plecnik_house.name: Plečnik House
plecnik_house.price_text: Small entry fee, check on the day
plecnik_house.tip: The home of the architect who shaped modern Ljubljana; book a guided slot ahead.

kranj_sausage.name: Kranjska klobasa (Carniolan sausage)
kranj_sausage.hours: Lunch and dinner at traditional restaurants
kranj_sausage.tip: Order it with mustard and rye bread at a riverside gostilna for a simple local meal.

potica.name: Potica (nut roll cake)
potica.price_text: ≈ EUR 3–6 per slice or small loaf
potica.tip: A traditional rolled cake; buy a slice with coffee or a small loaf to take home.

town_hall.name: Ljubljana Town Hall
town_hall.price_text: Free to view the courtyard and fountain
town_hall.hours: Weekday office hours; courtyard usually open
town_hall.tip: Step into the courtyard to see the baroque fountain; it is a quick stop on the Old Town walk.

robotic_bar.name: Riverside café terrace
robotic_bar.price_text: Coffee ≈ EUR 2–3 · drinks priced per menu
robotic_bar.tip: Grab a riverside table in the evening; the Ljubljanica embankment is the city's social heart.

national_gallery.name: National Gallery of Slovenia
national_gallery.price_text: Modest entry fee, check on the day
national_gallery.tip: Good for Slovenian art from the Middle Ages to the 20th century; pair it with nearby Tivoli Park.

lunch_market_food.name: Odprta kuhna street food market
lunch_market_food.hours: Usually Fridays in warmer months, daytime to early evening
lunch_market_food.tip: Local food trucks gather by the market; go early for shorter queues.

castle_funicular.name: Ljubljana Castle funicular
castle_funicular.price_text: Return ticket charged, check on the day
castle_funicular.hours: Roughly 09:00–21:00 in summer, shorter in winter
castle_funicular.tip: Saves the climb; combine the ticket with castle entry if you plan to visit the exhibitions.

stays.why: Step out into the pedestrian lanes, the river and the market. Quiet at night, close to everything.
The most central base: bridges, buses and cafés on the doorstep. Some street noise.
Cheapest beds, walk to the bus and train stations, and nightlife at Metelkova. A 15-minute walk to the centre.
Green and calm next to Tivoli Park; good for families and longer stays. A short bus or walk to the centre.

food: Try local dishes: štruklji (rolled dumplings), kranjska klobasa sausage, and potica nut roll for dessert.
The central market (Pogačarjev trg) has produce stalls and a covered market; some days bring street food and a morning food market — check on the day.
Riverside terraces along the Ljubljanica are the classic spot for a slow lunch or evening drink.
Cheap eats: burek bakeries and market snacks for a few euros; a sit-down lunch is often around €10–15.
Vegetarian and vegan options are common in the centre; book ahead for popular dinner spots on weekends.
more_time: Lake Bled is an easy day trip by bus or train (roughly 1–1.5 hours each way); go early to beat the crowds.
Postojna Cave and Predjama Castle make a full day out; book cave tickets ahead in summer.
Swap a city afternoon for a walk up Šmarna gora or a bike ride along the Ljubljanica for green views.
